metadata.description: Scenario-Based Study Companion for AZ-305 certification - validates expertise in designing cloud and hybrid solutions for identity, governance, data storage, business continuity, and infrastructure.

questions.title: Hybrid Identity Architecture
questions.scenario: A multinational company with 50,000 employees is migrating to Azure. They have on-premises Active Directory with complex GPOs, require seamless SSO to both cloud and on-premises apps, and must maintain existing security policies during migration.
questions.questionText: Which identity architecture should you recommend?

choices.text: Azure AD Connect with Password Hash Sync and Seamless SSO
Cloud-only Entra ID with manual user provisioning
Azure AD Connect with Pass-through Authentication only
Federation with AD FS for all authentication

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which sync method keeps authentication working even when on-premises infrastructure goes down?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AD Connect with Password Hash Sync (PHS) and Seamless SSO is the recommended approach. PHS provides resilience (works even if on-premises is down), enables leaked credential detection, and Seamless SSO provides frictionless sign-in from domain-joined devices without AD FS complexity.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• PHS is Microsoft's recommended default; it syncs password hashes (not actual passwords) to Entra ID.
  • Pass-through Authentication (PTA) validates against on-premises AD but adds dependency.
  • AD FS adds complexity and infrastructure; use only when federation is required (third-party MFA, smart cards).
  • PHS enables Identity Protection risk-based policies and leaked credential reports.

questions.title: Multi-tenant SaaS Identity
questions.scenario: You're designing a multi-tenant SaaS application. Each customer (tenant) wants their users to sign in with their own corporate Entra ID. Some customers require Conditional Access policies to apply.
questions.questionText: Which identity pattern should you implement?

choices.text: Azure AD B2C with local accounts for all users
Azure AD B2B with external identities and cross-tenant access policies
Single Entra ID tenant with all customer users as members
Separate Entra ID tenant per customer managed by you

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which identity model lets each tenant keep authenticating with their own corporate directory?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AD B2B allows customers to authenticate with their corporate Entra ID (home tenant) while your application manages authorization. Cross-tenant access policies let you control collaboration settings. Customer Conditional Access policies apply during authentication.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• B2B: Business-to-business, external users from other organizations; B2C: Consumer identities.
  • Cross-tenant access settings control inbound/outbound collaboration per organization.
  • B2B direct connect enables seamless Teams shared channels without guest accounts.
  • Multi-tenant app registration allows sign-in from any Entra ID tenant.

questions.title: Privileged Access Management
questions.scenario: Your organization needs to reduce standing administrative access. Admins should request elevated permissions only when needed, with approval workflows and time-limited access.
questions.questionText: Which solution should you implement?

choices.text: Conditional Access policies only
Custom approval workflow with Logic Apps
Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
Permanent role assignments with MFA

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which Azure service turns standing admin roles into on-demand, time-limited activations.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM) enables just-in-time (JIT) access to privileged roles. Users are eligible for roles but must activate them, optionally requiring approval, MFA, and justification. Access is time-limited and fully audited.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• PIM covers both Entra ID roles and Azure resource roles (RBAC).
  • Access reviews ensure ongoing validation of role assignments.
  • Alerts notify on suspicious activation patterns.
  • Requires Entra ID P2 license.

questions.title: Governance at Scale
questions.scenario: An enterprise with 200 subscriptions across multiple business units needs centralized governance. They require consistent tagging, allowed regions, and security baselines applied automatically to new subscriptions.
questions.questionText: What architecture should you design?

choices.text: Apply policies individually to each subscription
Management group hierarchy with Azure Policy initiatives and Blueprints
Single subscription with resource groups per business unit
ARM templates with governance resources in each deployment

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you apply governance rules once and have them automatically cascade to hundreds of subscriptions?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Design a management group hierarchy (e.g., Root > Platform/Landing Zones > Prod/NonProd > BU). Assign Azure Policy initiatives at appropriate scopes for automatic inheritance. Use Blueprints to deploy standard resources and policies to new subscriptions (landing zone pattern).

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Azure Landing Zone architecture provides proven management group structure.
  • Policy initiatives bundle related policies; built-in initiatives exist for common standards (CIS, NIST).
  • DeployIfNotExists policies can automatically remediate non-compliance.
  • Exemptions should be time-limited and tracked.

questions.title: Monitoring Strategy
questions.scenario: You need a unified monitoring solution for 500 VMs across multiple subscriptions, with centralized alerting, dashboards, and log retention for compliance (7 years for audit logs).
questions.questionText: What monitoring architecture should you design?

choices.text: Azure Monitor only without Log Analytics
Centralized Log Analytics workspace with Azure Monitor, archive to storage for long-term retention
Separate Log Analytics workspace per subscription
Third-party monitoring solution exclusively

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which approach unifies log queries across subscriptions while meeting a 7-year retention mandate cost-effectively.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Use a centralized Log Analytics workspace for operational data (up to 2 years interactive retention). Configure diagnostic settings to send logs from all resources. For 7-year compliance retention, export to Azure Storage (archive tier) or use Log Analytics data export.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Workspace design: centralized for small/medium; federated for large enterprises with data sovereignty needs.
  • Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) replaces legacy agents; supports Data Collection Rules.
  • Archive tier storage costs ~$0.002/GB/month for long-term retention.
  • Log Analytics workspace-based Application Insights recommended for new deployments.

questions.title: Relational Data Platform Selection
questions.scenario: A retail company needs to migrate a 10TB SQL Server database with 500+ stored procedures, CLR assemblies, and SQL Agent jobs. They want minimal code changes and full SQL Server feature compatibility.
questions.questionText: Which Azure data platform should you recommend?

choices.text: SQL Server on Azure VM
Azure SQL Database (single database)
Azure Database for PostgreSQL
Azure SQL Managed Instance

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which PaaS option preserves CLR assemblies, SQL Agent jobs, and stored procedures without OS management overhead?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure SQL Managed Instance offers near 100% compatibility with on-premises SQL Server, including SQL Agent, CLR, cross-database queries, and linked servers. It's a PaaS service so you don't manage OS or patching, unlike SQL on VM.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SQL MI supports up to 16TB storage; for larger, use SQL on VM or partition data.
  • Azure SQL Database lacks some features: CLR, SQL Agent, cross-database queries.
  • SQL on VM gives full control but requires you to manage HA, backups, and patching.
  • Use Azure Database Migration Service for online migrations with minimal downtime.

questions.title: NoSQL Database Selection
questions.scenario: A gaming company needs a database for player profiles and game state with single-digit millisecond reads globally. Players are distributed worldwide and need consistent experience regardless of location.
questions.questionText: Which database solution should you recommend?

choices.text: Azure Cosmos DB with multi-region writes
Azure Cache for Redis
Azure Table Storage
Azure SQL Database with geo-replication

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What kind of database offers guaranteed low-latency reads worldwide with built-in multi-region write capability?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Cosmos DB offers single-digit millisecond response times at any scale with 99.999% availability when using multi-region configuration. Multi-region writes allow players to write to their nearest region, eliminating write latency caused by geo-distance.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Choose appropriate consistency level: Session consistency often balances performance and correctness for gaming.
  • Partition key design is critical: choose a key with high cardinality and even distribution.
  • Multi-region writes require conflict resolution policy (Last Writer Wins or custom).
  • Consider serverless for variable/unpredictable workloads; provisioned throughput for steady-state.

questions.title: Data Lake Architecture
questions.scenario: An analytics team needs to store petabytes of raw data (logs, IoT telemetry, documents) for big data processing with Spark and machine learning workloads.
questions.questionText: Which storage solution should you design?

choices.text: Azure Blob Storage without hierarchical namespace
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 with hierarchical namespace
Azure Files Premium
Azure SQL Data Warehouse

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Big data frameworks like Spark need directory-level operations. Which storage option adds file-system semantics at blob scale?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 is built on Blob Storage with hierarchical namespace enabled. This provides file system semantics (directories, atomic operations) required for big data frameworks like Spark, Hadoop, and Databricks while maintaining Blob Storage's massive scale and cost efficiency.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Hierarchical namespace enables efficient directory operations (rename, delete).
  • ABFS driver optimized for analytics workloads.
  • Use ACLs for fine-grained access control in addition to RBAC.
  • Organize data in zones: raw, enriched, curated (medallion architecture).

questions.title: Storage Account Security
questions.scenario: A healthcare application stores PHI (Protected Health Information) in Blob Storage. Requirements: data must be encrypted with customer-managed keys, accessible only from specific VNets, and all access must be audited.
questions.questionText: Which combination of features should you configure?

choices.text: Customer-managed keys in Key Vault, Private Endpoints, Storage Analytics logging
Microsoft-managed keys, Service Endpoints, no logging
Customer-managed keys, public access with SAS tokens, diagnostic logging
Infrastructure encryption only, firewall rules, Activity Log only

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about three layers: who controls the encryption keys, how traffic stays off the public internet, and how every access is recorded.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Use customer-managed keys (CMK) in Azure Key Vault for encryption key control. Private Endpoints provide private IP access from your VNet without internet exposure. Enable Storage Analytics logging or Azure Monitor diagnostic settings to audit all read/write operations.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• CMK allows key rotation and revocation; consider double encryption (infrastructure + CMK).
  • Private Endpoints vs Service Endpoints: PE provides private IP; SE routes over Microsoft backbone but uses public IP.
  • Disable public blob access at the storage account level for sensitive data.
  • Enable soft delete and versioning for data protection.

questions.title: Caching Strategy
questions.scenario: An e-commerce site experiences high database load from repeated queries for product catalog data. Product data changes infrequently but reads are extremely high during sales events.
questions.questionText: What caching architecture should you implement?

choices.text: In-memory caching on each app instance only
Azure Cache for Redis with cache-aside pattern and TTL-based expiration
Azure CDN for all API responses
Database query result caching only

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which caching approach works across all app instances and lets the application control when data enters and expires from the cache?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Cache for Redis provides a distributed, in-memory cache. Use the cache-aside pattern: check cache first, on miss read from database and populate cache with TTL. This reduces database load while ensuring data freshness through expiration.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Cache-aside: application manages cache; write-through: writes go to cache and DB together.
  • Consider cache warming before sales events to prevent thundering herd.
  • Use Redis data structures (sorted sets, hashes) for complex scenarios.
  • Premium tier provides clustering, geo-replication, and persistence.

questions.title: Message-based Integration
questions.scenario: An order processing system needs to decouple order placement from fulfillment. Orders must never be lost, processing must be exactly-once, and the system must handle 10,000 orders/second during peak.
questions.questionText: Which messaging solution should you design?

choices.text: Azure Event Grid
Azure Service Bus Premium with sessions and duplicate detection
Azure Queue Storage
Azure Event Hubs

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The scenario demands guaranteed delivery and exactly-once semantics. Which messaging tier supports sessions and duplicate detection?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Service Bus Premium tier provides high throughput (up to millions of messages/day), guaranteed delivery, and enterprise features. Sessions enable ordered processing and exactly-once semantics. Duplicate detection prevents reprocessing if producers retry.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Service Bus: transactional messaging; Event Hubs: high-throughput event streaming.
  • Sessions group related messages and provide FIFO within a session.
  • Dead-letter queue handles poison messages.
  • Premium tier provides dedicated resources, 1MB messages, and geo-DR.

questions.title: Event Streaming Architecture
questions.scenario: An IoT platform ingests telemetry from 1 million devices sending data every second. Data needs real-time processing for anomaly detection and long-term storage for analytics.
questions.questionText: What architecture should you design?

choices.text: Azure Event Hubs with Azure Stream Analytics and ADLS Gen2
Azure Service Bus with Azure Functions
Azure Queue Storage with batch processing
Azure IoT Hub only with direct database writes

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the pipeline: massive event ingestion, real-time anomaly queries on the stream, and a landing zone for long-term analytics.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Event Hubs can ingest millions of events/second with low latency. Azure Stream Analytics processes streams in real-time using SQL-like queries for anomaly detection. Event Hubs Capture or Stream Analytics outputs to ADLS Gen2 for long-term storage and batch analytics.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Event Hubs partitions enable parallel processing; partition key distributes events.
  • Consider IoT Hub for device management features (twins, direct methods, provisioning).
  • Event Hubs Capture automatically writes to storage in Avro format.
  • Kafka protocol support allows existing Kafka applications to use Event Hubs.

questions.title: Multi-Region DR Strategy
questions.scenario: A financial services application requires RPO of 5 minutes and RTO of 1 hour. The application uses Azure SQL Database and App Service. Cost optimization is important but must not compromise recovery objectives.
questions.questionText: Which disaster recovery architecture should you design?

choices.text: Active-passive with Azure SQL geo-replication and standby App Service Plan
Single region with availability zones only
Backup and restore only
Active-active with Traffic Manager and synchronized databases

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What DR topology keeps a standby region at low cost while still meeting a 5-minute RPO and 1-hour RTO?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure SQL active geo-replication continuously replicates to a secondary region (RPO ~5 seconds). Deploy App Service in the secondary region at minimum scale (cost optimization), scale up during failover. Use Azure Traffic Manager or Front Door for automatic failover detection.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Geo-replication RPO depends on network latency; typically under 5 seconds.
  • Auto-failover groups automate failover for SQL Database.
  • App Service deployment slots can pre-warm the standby environment.
  • Test failover regularly; document runbooks for DR procedures.

questions.title: Backup Strategy Design
questions.scenario: An organization needs comprehensive backup for Azure VMs, SQL databases, file shares, and blob data. Backups must be retained for 7 years for compliance, with some data requiring immutable storage.
questions.questionText: What backup architecture should you implement?

choices.text: Third-party backup solution exclusively
Azure Backup with Recovery Services Vault, long-term retention policies, and immutable vaults
VM snapshots stored in the same region only
Application-level backups to blob storage without centralized management

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which native service gives you a single pane for VM, SQL, and file backups with 7-year retention and tamper-proof storage?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Backup with Recovery Services Vault provides centralized backup for VMs, SQL, Files, and blobs. Configure backup policies with long-term retention (up to 99 years). Enable immutable vaults to protect backups from deletion or modification (ransomware protection).

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Backup Center provides single-pane management across vaults and subscriptions.
  • GRS vault replication protects backups from regional disaster.
  • Immutable vaults prevent backup deletion even by administrators.
  • MARS agent backs up on-premises files; DPM/MABS for complex on-premises workloads.

questions.title: High Availability for VMs
questions.scenario: A mission-critical SAP HANA database requires 99.99% availability. The VM must survive datacenter-level failures within a region and have predictable low-latency storage.
questions.questionText: Which VM deployment configuration should you design?

choices.text: Virtual Machine Scale Set in single zone
Single VM with Premium SSD
Availability Zones with Ultra Disks or Premium SSD v2
Availability Set with Standard HDD

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What deployment model survives a datacenter failure within a region and pairs it with storage that meets HANA latency demands?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Deploy VMs across Availability Zones for 99.99% SLA and datacenter-level fault tolerance. Use Ultra Disks or Premium SSD v2 for SAP HANA's demanding storage requirements (consistent sub-millisecond latency, high IOPS). Zone-redundant disks replicate across zones.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Availability Zones: 99.99% SLA; Availability Sets: 99.95% SLA; Single VM with Premium: 99.9%.
  • Ultra Disks: up to 160,000 IOPS and 4,000 MBps per disk.
  • Zone-redundant storage (ZRS) for managed disks provides zone redundancy.
  • SAP HANA certified M-series VMs for production workloads.

questions.title: Azure Site Recovery Design
questions.scenario: A company needs to replicate on-premises VMware VMs to Azure for disaster recovery. They want automated failover with minimal RTO and the ability to test DR without impacting production.
questions.questionText: How should you design the replication?

choices.text: Azure Site Recovery with recovery plans and isolated test failover network
Manual VM exports and imports during disaster
Azure Migrate for one-time migration only
Backup and restore from Recovery Services Vault

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service continuously replicates on-premises VMs to Azure and lets you test failover without affecting production?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Site Recovery (ASR) continuously replicates VMware VMs to Azure. Recovery plans orchestrate failover sequence with scripts and manual actions. Test failover creates VMs in an isolated network without affecting replication or production, enabling regular DR drills.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• ASR supports VMware, Hyper-V, physical servers, and Azure-to-Azure replication.
  • Recovery plans group VMs and define failover order with custom scripts.
  • Application-consistent snapshots ensure database integrity.
  • Replication frequency: continuous (Hyper-V/VMware) or every 5/15/30 minutes.

questions.title: Hub-Spoke Network Topology
questions.scenario: An enterprise needs to connect 20 spoke VNets to shared services (firewall, DNS, AD) while maintaining network isolation between business units. Traffic between spokes must be inspected.
questions.questionText: Which network architecture should you design?

choices.text: Hub-spoke with Azure Firewall in hub and UDRs routing spoke-to-spoke traffic through hub
Full mesh VNet peering between all VNets
Single large VNet with subnets for each business unit
Separate VNets with VPN connections between them

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you share a central firewall across 20 isolated VNets while ensuring all inter-VNet traffic is inspected?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Hub-spoke topology places shared services (Azure Firewall, DNS, NVAs) in a central hub VNet. Spokes peer to hub only, providing isolation. User-defined routes (UDRs) on spoke subnets route all traffic through Azure Firewall for inspection and logging.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Enable "Allow Gateway Transit" on hub and "Use Remote Gateway" on spokes for on-premises connectivity.
  • Azure Virtual WAN simplifies large hub-spoke deployments with managed hubs.
  • Azure Firewall Manager provides centralized policy management.
  • Consider Azure Route Server for dynamic routing with NVAs.

questions.title: Hybrid Connectivity Design
questions.scenario: A company requires dedicated private connectivity from their datacenter to Azure with 10 Gbps bandwidth, redundancy, and the ability to connect to multiple Azure regions.
questions.questionText: Which connectivity solution should you design?

choices.text: Azure Peering Service
ExpressRoute with Global Reach and redundant circuits
Point-to-site VPN for all users
Site-to-site VPN only

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The scenario requires dedicated private bandwidth at 10 Gbps with multi-region reach. What type of connection fits?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: ExpressRoute provides dedicated private connectivity with predictable performance. Deploy redundant circuits (different providers/locations) for high availability. ExpressRoute Global Reach allows traffic to flow between on-premises sites through Microsoft's network, connecting multiple regions.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• ExpressRoute circuits: 50 Mbps to 100 Gbps; Direct provides 10/100 Gbps port.
  • Premium add-on enables global routing and more VNet connections.
  • ExpressRoute is not encrypted by default; layer VPN for encryption if needed.
  • Consider ExpressRoute + VPN failover for maximum resiliency.

questions.title: Web Application Architecture
questions.scenario: A global web application requires sub-100ms response times for users worldwide, SSL offloading, WAF protection, and intelligent routing to the nearest healthy backend.
questions.questionText: Which Azure services should you combine?

choices.text: Azure Front Door with WAF policy and backend pools in multiple regions
Azure Load Balancer only
Azure Traffic Manager with Application Gateway per region
Azure CDN only

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which global Layer 7 service combines SSL offloading, web-app firewall protection, and latency-based routing to backends?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Front Door is a global Layer 7 load balancer with anycast (users connect to nearest edge). It provides SSL offloading, integrated WAF, intelligent routing based on latency/priority/weighted, and health probes. Backend pools can span Azure regions and even external endpoints.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Front Door vs Traffic Manager: Front Door is Layer 7 with data path; Traffic Manager is DNS-based.
  • Front Door Standard/Premium tiers include CDN integration.
  • WAF policies protect against OWASP top 10 and bot attacks.
  • Private Link origins allow Front Door to connect to private backends.

questions.title: Container Platform Selection
questions.scenario: A team is containerizing 50 microservices. They need service discovery, automatic scaling, rolling deployments, secrets management, and integration with Azure services. The team has Kubernetes experience.
questions.questionText: Which container platform should you recommend?

choices.text: Azure App Service for Containers
Azure Container Instances for all services
Self-managed Kubernetes on VMs
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) with managed add-ons

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The team already knows Kubernetes. Which Azure platform manages the control plane so they can focus on workloads?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: AKS is the managed Kubernetes service with Azure handling the control plane. Managed add-ons provide service mesh (Istio), monitoring (Azure Monitor), secrets (Key Vault CSI driver), and GitOps (Flux). The team's Kubernetes experience transfers directly.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• AKS control plane is free; pay only for worker nodes.
  • KEDA provides event-driven autoscaling beyond HPA.
  • Azure CNI vs Kubenet: CNI gives pods VNet IPs; Kubenet uses NAT.
  • AKS workload identity replaces pod identity for Azure AD integration.

questions.title: Serverless Application Design
questions.scenario: An application processes uploaded documents: extract text, analyze sentiment, store results. Processing should scale to zero when idle and handle burst uploads. Costs must be minimized.
questions.questionText: Which architecture should you design?

choices.text: Always-running VMs polling for new files
App Service with scheduled jobs
Azure Batch for all processing
Azure Functions (Consumption) triggered by Blob Storage, using Cognitive Services, output to Cosmos DB

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which compute model scales to zero when idle and bills only for actual execution time during bursts?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Functions on Consumption plan scales automatically based on events (blob trigger). It scales to zero when idle, minimizing costs. Integrate with Cognitive Services for text extraction (Form Recognizer) and sentiment analysis (Language). Store structured results in Cosmos DB.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Consumption plan: pay per execution; 5-minute default timeout (10 max).
  • Use Durable Functions for long-running or stateful workflows.
  • Consider Premium plan for VNet integration and longer execution times.
  • Blob trigger uses Storage queues internally; consider Event Grid trigger for lower latency.

questions.title: API Management Design
questions.scenario: A company exposes APIs to partners and internal developers. Requirements: rate limiting, authentication via OAuth, versioning, developer portal, and analytics on API usage.
questions.questionText: Which service should be the centerpiece of the API architecture?

choices.text: Azure Functions with HTTP triggers only
Custom API gateway built on App Service
Azure Front Door only
Azure API Management with policies and developer portal

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which service handles rate limiting, OAuth validation, versioning, and a developer portal in one place.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure API Management (APIM) provides API gateway, developer portal, and management plane. Policies handle rate limiting, JWT validation, transformation, and caching. Built-in analytics show usage patterns. Products and subscriptions control access levels.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• APIM tiers: Consumption (serverless), Developer, Basic, Standard, Premium.
  • Premium provides multi-region deployment and VNet integration.
  • Self-hosted gateway extends APIM to on-premises or other clouds.
  • Versioning strategies: path, query string, or header-based.

questions.title: Compute Cost Optimization
questions.scenario: A batch processing workload runs nightly for 4 hours, processing large datasets. The workload is fault-tolerant and can be interrupted. Cost is the primary concern.
questions.questionText: Which compute strategy should you recommend?

choices.text: Reserved Instances for 3 years
Dedicated Hosts
Pay-as-you-go VMs running 24/7
Azure Spot Virtual Machines with checkpointing

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: The workload is fault-tolerant and short-lived. Which VM pricing model maximizes savings for interruptible jobs?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Spot VMs use spare Azure capacity at up to 90% discount. Since the workload is fault-tolerant and runs only 4 hours, Spot is ideal. Implement checkpointing to save progress and resume if evicted. Reserved Instances suit steady-state workloads, not intermittent ones.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Spot VMs can be evicted with 30 seconds notice when Azure needs capacity.
  • Set max price to control costs; use -1 for market price.
  • Eviction policy: Stop-Deallocate (resume later) or Delete.
  • Azure Batch natively supports Spot VMs with automatic retry.

questions.title: VM Scale Set Design
questions.scenario: A web tier needs to handle variable traffic, automatically scaling between 2-20 instances. Instances must be distributed across fault domains, and deployments should not cause downtime.
questions.questionText: How should you configure the scale set?

choices.text: VMSS Uniform with manual instance management
Manual scaling with availability set
Individual VMs with custom scaling scripts
VMSS with Flexible orchestration, autoscale rules, and rolling upgrade policy

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which scale set orchestration mode supports fault-domain spreading, metric-based autoscale, and zero-downtime rolling updates?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: VM Scale Sets with Flexible orchestration spread instances across fault domains automatically. Configure autoscale rules based on metrics (CPU, memory, queue depth) with min/max instance counts. Rolling upgrade policy updates instances in batches, maintaining availability during deployments.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Flexible vs Uniform: Flexible offers more VM features and mixing; Uniform is simpler.
  • Overprovisioning reduces scale-out time but may incur brief extra costs.
  • Health probes with automatic repair replace unhealthy instances.
  • Instance protection prevents specific instances from scale-in/updates.

questions.title: Workload Identity
questions.scenario: Applications running in AKS need to access Azure Key Vault and Storage without storing credentials in code or configuration.
questions.questionText: Which identity solution should you implement?

choices.text: Managed Identity for VM only
Store service principal credentials in Kubernetes secrets
Azure AD Workload Identity with federated credentials
Shared access signatures hardcoded in application

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can Kubernetes pods obtain Azure tokens without any stored secrets or service principal credentials?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AD Workload Identity federates Kubernetes service accounts with Azure AD. Pods use projected service account tokens to authenticate, eliminating credential management. Grant the workload identity Azure RBAC roles for Key Vault and Storage access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Workload Identity replaces the deprecated AAD Pod Identity.
  • Uses OIDC federation; no secrets stored in cluster.
  • Create federated credential linking Kubernetes SA to Azure AD app registration.
  • Works with any workload supporting OIDC token exchange.

questions.title: Data Integration Architecture
questions.scenario: A data platform needs to ingest data from 50+ sources (databases, SaaS apps, files), transform it, and load into a data warehouse. Pipelines should be visual, manageable, and cost-effective.
questions.questionText: Which service should orchestrate the data integration?

choices.text: Custom ETL code on VMs
SQL Server Integration Services on Azure VM
Azure Logic Apps only
Azure Data Factory with integration runtimes and mapping data flows

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which managed service connects to 50+ diverse source types and provides visual pipeline authoring for ETL/ELT?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Data Factory (ADF) is a managed data integration service with 100+ built-in connectors. Mapping data flows provide visual transformation logic executed on Spark. Integration runtimes connect to on-premises and cloud sources. Pay only for pipeline execution time.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Self-hosted Integration Runtime enables on-premises connectivity.
  • Data flows execute on Spark clusters; enable debug for development.
  • Use triggers for scheduling, event-based, or tumbling window patterns.
  • Synapse Pipelines provides similar capabilities integrated with Synapse Analytics.

questions.title: Analytics Platform Design
questions.scenario: A company needs a unified analytics platform for data warehousing, big data processing, and machine learning. Data scientists want to use Spark notebooks; analysts want SQL access.
questions.questionText: Which platform should you design around?

choices.text: Separate Azure SQL Database and HDInsight clusters
Azure Synapse Analytics with dedicated SQL pool, serverless SQL, and Spark pools
Azure Databricks only
SQL Server on Azure VM with SSIS

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which platform unifies SQL warehousing, Spark notebooks, and pipeline orchestration under a single workspace?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Synapse Analytics integrates dedicated SQL pools (data warehouse), serverless SQL (query data lake directly), and Spark pools (big data/ML) in a unified workspace. Analysts use SQL; data scientists use Spark notebooks. Synapse Pipelines handles orchestration.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Dedicated SQL pool: provisioned MPP warehouse; serverless: pay-per-query.
  • Synapse Link provides near-real-time analytics on operational data (Cosmos DB, SQL).
  • Workspace managed VNet provides network isolation.
  • Consider Databricks for advanced ML and Delta Lake capabilities.

questions.title: Zero Trust Network Access
questions.scenario: Remote workers need secure access to internal web applications without VPN. Access should verify user identity, device compliance, and apply least-privilege per application.
questions.questionText: Which solution enables zero trust application access?

choices.text: Expose applications directly to internet with firewall
Site-to-site VPN for all users
Remote Desktop Gateway
Azure AD Application Proxy with Conditional Access

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can remote users reach internal web apps without a VPN while still enforcing device compliance and MFA per application?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AD Application Proxy publishes on-premises web applications without inbound firewall rules or VPN. Users authenticate through Azure AD, enabling Conditional Access policies (MFA, compliant device, location). Each application can have individual access policies.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• App Proxy Connector runs on-premises; outbound-only communication to Azure.
  • Pre-authentication options: Azure AD (recommended) or passthrough.
  • Supports header-based, Kerberos, and password-based SSO to backend apps.
  • Consider Microsoft Entra Private Access for broader zero trust network access.

questions.title: Landing Zone Architecture
questions.scenario: An enterprise is adopting Azure at scale. They need a standardized foundation with networking, identity, governance, and security that supports autonomous workload teams.
questions.questionText: What should be your starting point for the architecture?

choices.text: Manual setup of each component independently
Azure Landing Zone accelerator with platform and application landing zones
Third-party infrastructure automation only
Single subscription for all workloads

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What Microsoft-published reference architecture provides a ready-made foundation for networking, identity, and governance at scale?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Landing Zone accelerator provides a conceptual architecture and reference implementations for enterprise-scale Azure adoption. It includes management group hierarchy, policies, hub networking, identity integration, and subscription vending for workload teams.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Platform landing zones: shared services (connectivity, identity, management).
  • Application landing zones: workload subscriptions with inherited governance.
  • Subscription vending automates new subscription provisioning with policies.
  • Cloud Adoption Framework provides guidance; Landing Zone accelerators provide implementation.

questions.title: Application Resilience Patterns
questions.scenario: A microservices application needs to handle transient failures gracefully, prevent cascade failures, and maintain responsiveness when downstream services are slow.
questions.questionText: Which resilience patterns should the architecture implement?

choices.text: No error handling; let failures propagate
Synchronous retry loops without delay
Retry with exponential backoff, circuit breaker, and timeout patterns
Single point of failure with no redundancy

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which classic resilience patterns address transient faults, cascade failures, and slow-downstream hangs respectively?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Retry with exponential backoff handles transient failures without overwhelming services. Circuit breaker pattern stops calling failing services, allowing recovery. Timeouts prevent indefinite waiting. Together, these patterns create resilient applications that degrade gracefully.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Add jitter to retries to prevent thundering herd.
  • Circuit breaker states: Closed (normal), Open (failing), Half-Open (testing recovery).
  • Bulkhead pattern isolates failures to prevent resource exhaustion.
  • Libraries: Polly (.NET), Resilience4j (Java), or service mesh (Istio/Linkerd).

questions.title: Private Endpoint Design
questions.scenario: All PaaS services (Storage, SQL, Key Vault) must be accessible only from your VNet. No traffic should traverse the public internet.
questions.questionText: How should you design the network connectivity?

choices.text: Service Endpoints only
Private Endpoints for each service with Private DNS zones
Firewall rules allowing VNet IP ranges
Public endpoints with SAS authentication

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How do you give PaaS services a private IP inside your VNet so traffic never touches the public internet?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Private Endpoints create a network interface with a private IP in your VNet for PaaS services. Traffic stays entirely on Microsoft's network. Private DNS zones ensure service FQDNs resolve to private IPs from your VNet. Disable public network access on services.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Private Endpoint vs Service Endpoint: PE has private IP; SE uses public IP over Microsoft backbone.
  • Centralize Private DNS zones in hub and link to spoke VNets.
  • Azure Private Link service exposes your own services privately.
  • NSG on Private Endpoint subnet controls access (supported for most services).

questions.title: Database Partitioning Strategy
questions.scenario: A multi-tenant SaaS application stores tenant data in Azure SQL Database. Tenants vary greatly in size (1GB to 1TB). You need to balance cost, performance isolation, and management overhead.
questions.questionText: What partitioning strategy should you implement?

choices.text: Elastic pools with tenant-per-database and tiered pools by size
Separate SQL Server per tenant
Single database with tenant ID column
Cosmos DB with single partition key

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you isolate each tenant in its own database while sharing compute resources cost-effectively across variable-size tenants?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Use database-per-tenant for isolation and easy management (backup, restore, move). Group databases into elastic pools to share resources efficiently. Create tiered pools (small/medium/large) and place tenants based on their size. Move large tenants to dedicated databases.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Elastic pools: tenants share eDTUs/vCores; burst within pool limits.
  • Elastic Jobs runs maintenance across pooled databases.
  • Shard Map Manager routes connections in sharded applications.
  • Consider Hyperscale for very large tenants (100TB+ support).

questions.title: DevOps Integration
questions.scenario: Development teams need to provision environments on-demand, deploy applications through pipelines, and enforce infrastructure standards. Infrastructure must be versioned and repeatable.
questions.questionText: What infrastructure-as-code approach should you standardize on?

choices.text: Bicep templates in Git with CI/CD pipelines and Azure Policy guardrails
ARM templates emailed between teams
Manual portal deployments documented in wiki
PowerShell scripts with hardcoded values

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What combination of declarative IaC language, version control, and automated pipelines makes infrastructure repeatable and auditable?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Bicep is a domain-specific language that compiles to ARM templates with cleaner syntax. Store templates in Git for version control and code review. CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions) automate deployments. Azure Policy ensures deployed resources comply with standards.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Bicep modules enable reusable, composable infrastructure components.
  • Deployment stacks manage lifecycle of template-deployed resources.
  • What-if operations preview changes before deployment.
  • Consider Terraform for multi-cloud IaC requirements.

questions.title: Security Architecture
questions.scenario: A defense-in-depth security architecture is required. The application handles sensitive data and must meet SOC 2 compliance with centralized security monitoring.
questions.questionText: Which combination of services provides comprehensive security?

choices.text: Network Security Groups only
Azure Firewall without logging
Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, and Key Vault with managed HSM
Third-party antivirus on VMs only

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Defense in depth needs posture assessment, centralized security event correlation, and hardware-protected key storage. Which trio covers all three?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Defender for Cloud provides security posture management and workload protection. Microsoft Sentinel provides cloud-native SIEM/SOAR for centralized security monitoring and automated response. Azure Key Vault with managed HSM provides FIPS 140-2 Level 3 key protection.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard tracks SOC 2, PCI-DSS, etc.
  • Sentinel uses Log Analytics; connect Defender, Azure AD, and custom sources.
  • Managed HSM provides dedicated HSM for high-security key operations.
  • Use Azure Policy to enforce security configurations continuously.

questions.title: SLA Composition
questions.scenario: Your application uses Azure App Service (99.95% SLA) connecting to Azure SQL Database (99.99% SLA). Both must be available for the application to work.
questions.questionText: What is the composite SLA for the application?

choices.text: 99.95% (take the lowest)
99.94% (multiply individual SLAs)
99.99% (take the highest)
199.94% (add SLAs together)

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: When two services must both be up for the app to work, how does the overall availability relate to their individual SLAs?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: When services are in series (both required), multiply their SLAs: 99.95% x 99.99% = 99.94%. Each additional required component reduces overall SLA. To improve composite SLA, add redundancy (parallel paths) or use higher-SLA service tiers.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Parallel (redundant) paths improve SLA: 1 - (1 - SLA1) x (1 - SLA2).
  • More components in series = lower composite SLA.
  • Design for failure: assume components will fail and plan accordingly.
  • Application-level resilience can compensate for infrastructure SLA gaps.

questions.title: DNS Architecture
questions.scenario: Your hybrid environment requires unified DNS resolution: Azure resources must resolve on-premises names, and on-premises must resolve Azure Private Endpoint names.
questions.questionText: What DNS architecture should you implement?

choices.text: Hosts file entries on all machines
Custom DNS servers on VMs with conditional forwarders
Azure Private DNS Resolver with inbound and outbound endpoints
Public DNS only

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you enable bidirectional DNS resolution between Azure private zones and on-premises without running your own DNS VMs?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Private DNS Resolver provides inbound endpoints (on-premises resolves Azure private DNS) and outbound endpoints (Azure VNets resolve on-premises DNS). This eliminates the need for custom DNS VMs while enabling hybrid DNS resolution.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Inbound endpoint: on-premises forwards queries to Azure private zones.
  • Outbound endpoint with DNS forwarding ruleset: Azure forwards to on-premises DNS.
  • Link Private DNS zones to hub VNet; use DNS Resolver for cross-premises.
  • Consider Azure Firewall DNS proxy for centralized DNS with FQDN filtering.

questions.title: Data Encryption Strategy
questions.scenario: Regulations require encryption at rest with customer-controlled keys, encryption in transit, and the ability to prove data was never accessed by the cloud provider.
questions.questionText: What encryption architecture meets these requirements?

choices.text: Microsoft-managed keys only
No encryption with network isolation
Application-level encryption only
Customer-managed keys with Azure Confidential Computing for sensitive workloads

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Beyond encrypting data at rest and in transit, how do you prove the cloud provider itself cannot access data while it is being processed?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Customer-managed keys (CMK) in Key Vault provide control over encryption keys. For proving data isolation even from the provider, Azure Confidential Computing uses hardware-based trusted execution environments (TEEs) with remote attestation to verify code integrity.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• CMK: customer controls key lifecycle, rotation, and revocation.
  • Double encryption: infrastructure encryption + CMK for defense in depth.
  • Confidential VMs use AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX for memory encryption.
  • Azure Attestation verifies TEE integrity before processing sensitive data.

questions.title: Multi-region Deployment
questions.scenario: A globally distributed application requires active-active deployment across regions with automatic failover. Users should always connect to the nearest healthy region.
questions.questionText: Which traffic management approach should you use?

choices.text: Round-robin DNS
Azure Front Door with priority and latency-based routing
Azure Load Balancer across regions
Manual DNS updates during failover

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which global service uses anycast to route users to the nearest healthy backend with automatic failover?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Front Door provides global Layer 7 load balancing with health probes. Latency-based routing directs users to the nearest healthy backend. Priority settings enable automatic failover to secondary regions. Anycast ensures users connect to the nearest edge location.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Front Door supports weighted, latency, priority, and session affinity routing.
  • Health probes detect failures; failover is automatic and fast.
  • Consider Traffic Manager for DNS-based routing if Layer 7 isn't needed.
  • Active-active requires conflict resolution strategy for databases (e.g., Cosmos DB multi-write).

questions.title: Service Principal Security
questions.scenario: CI/CD pipelines need to deploy Azure resources. You want to avoid storing secrets and enable time-limited, auditable deployments.
questions.questionText: What authentication approach should the pipelines use?

choices.text: Personal access tokens of developers
Service principal with client secret stored in pipeline variables
Workload identity federation with OIDC from the CI/CD platform
Shared admin credentials

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can a CI/CD pipeline authenticate to Azure without storing any client secrets or certificates?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Workload identity federation allows CI/CD platforms (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps) to authenticate to Azure using OIDC tokens without stored secrets. Configure a federated credential on an Azure AD application that trusts tokens from the CI/CD provider.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• GitHub Actions: configure subject claim with repo, branch, and environment.
  • Azure DevOps: service connections support workload identity federation.
  • Tokens are short-lived; no secrets to rotate or leak.
  • Restrict federated credentials to specific repos/branches for security.

questions.title: Real-time Data Architecture
questions.scenario: A trading platform needs sub-second data freshness from operational database to analytics dashboards. The operational database is Azure Cosmos DB.
questions.questionText: What architecture provides near-real-time analytics without impacting operational workload?

choices.text: Manual data exports
Periodic ETL jobs every hour
Direct queries against Cosmos DB from Power BI
Azure Synapse Link for Cosmos DB with serverless SQL pool

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you run analytics on operational Cosmos DB data in near-real-time without ETL and without consuming transactional throughput?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Synapse Link automatically replicates Cosmos DB data to a columnar analytical store without ETL. Changes sync within seconds. Serverless SQL pool or Spark can query the analytical store without impacting transactional workload. Power BI connects for dashboards.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Analytical store uses column-oriented format optimized for analytics.
  • No RU consumption for analytical queries; separate from transactional store.
  • Analytical TTL can differ from transactional TTL.
  • Synapse Link also available for SQL Server and Dataverse.

questions.title: Network Security Design
questions.scenario: Web applications need protection against OWASP top 10, DDoS attacks, and must have centralized network policy enforcement across all workloads.
questions.questionText: What combination of network security services should you deploy?

choices.text: Azure Front Door with WAF, Azure DDoS Protection Standard, and Azure Firewall
Network Security Groups only
Application Gateway without WAF
Third-party firewall without Azure integration

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Three layers needed: Layer 7 app-attack protection, volumetric attack mitigation, and centralized network-level policy. What combination covers all three?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Front Door (or Application Gateway) with WAF protects against OWASP top 10 and bot attacks at Layer 7. DDoS Protection Standard provides enhanced protection with attack telemetry. Azure Firewall in hub VNet provides centralized Layer 3-7 network policy enforcement.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• WAF policies: managed rules for OWASP, bot protection, custom rules.
  • DDoS Standard: adaptive tuning, attack analytics, cost protection guarantee.
  • Azure Firewall Premium: TLS inspection, IDPS, URL filtering.
  • NSGs complement but don't replace firewall; NSGs are per-subnet/NIC.

questions.title: Entitlement Management
questions.scenario: External partners need temporary access to specific Azure resources and applications. Access should be self-service, time-limited, and automatically removed when the project ends.
questions.questionText: Which solution provides governed access lifecycle?

choices.text: Azure AD Entitlement Management with access packages
Manual guest user invitations with no expiration
Shared accounts for partners
VPN access to everything

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Azure AD feature lets external partners self-request bundled access that automatically expires when the project ends?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AD Entitlement Management creates access packages bundling group memberships, app access, and SharePoint sites. External users request access through a portal; policies control approval workflows and automatic expiration. Access reviews ensure ongoing validity.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Connected organizations enable streamlined access for known partners.
  • Policies define who can request, approvers, duration, and extensions.
  • Separation of duties: requestor can't be sole approver.
  • Requires Entra ID P2 license.

questions.title: Search Architecture
questions.scenario: An e-commerce platform needs full-text search with faceted navigation, typo tolerance, and relevance tuning. The catalog has 10 million products.
questions.questionText: Which service should power the search functionality?

choices.text: In-memory filtering in application
SQL Server full-text search
Cosmos DB with LIKE queries
Azure AI Search (Cognitive Search) with custom scoring profiles

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which managed search service supports faceted navigation, typo tolerance, and custom relevance scoring at scale?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AI Search (formerly Cognitive Search) is a managed search-as-a-service. It provides full-text search with analyzers, faceted navigation for filtering, fuzzy matching for typo tolerance, and scoring profiles for relevance tuning. Indexers sync data from various sources.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Semantic search uses AI for natural language understanding (Premium feature).
  • Vector search enables hybrid search with embeddings.
  • AI enrichment pipeline extracts insights from unstructured content.
  • Replicas provide query scale; partitions provide index size scale.

questions.title: Bastion and Secure Access
questions.scenario: Administrators need to access VMs in private subnets without public IPs or VPN. Access must be audited and time-limited.
questions.questionText: What solution provides secure VM access?

choices.text: Azure Bastion with just-in-time VM access from Defender for Cloud
Always-on VPN for all administrators
Jump box VM with permanent public IP
Public IPs on all VMs with NSG rules

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can admins reach private VMs via browser without exposing public IPs, and only when access is explicitly approved?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Bastion provides secure RDP/SSH access through the browser without exposing public IPs on VMs. Just-in-time (JIT) VM access from Defender for Cloud temporarily opens NSG rules for a specific source IP and duration. Combine for defense in depth.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Bastion Standard tier supports native client, file transfer, and scaling.
  • Bastion Premium adds session recording and private-only deployment.
  • JIT audits every access request; integrates with PIM for approval workflow.
  • Bastion can be shared across peered VNets.

questions.title: Data Consistency in Distributed Systems
questions.scenario: A globally distributed application needs data consistency. Some operations require strong consistency; others can tolerate eventual consistency for better performance.
questions.questionText: How should you design the data layer?

choices.text: Eventual consistency for everything
Local caching without database consistency
Strong consistency everywhere regardless of latency
Cosmos DB with session consistency default and strong consistency for critical operations

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which database lets you pick different consistency guarantees per operation, so critical writes get strong consistency while reads stay fast?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Cosmos DB provides five consistency levels: Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session, Consistent Prefix, and Eventual. Session consistency (default) guarantees read-your-writes and is suitable for most operations. Override to Strong for critical operations like financial transactions.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Strong consistency doubles RU cost and adds latency for global writes.
  • Session consistency uses session tokens; works well for user-specific data.
  • Bounded Staleness guarantees maximum lag (time or operations).
  • Consistency can be relaxed per-request but not strengthened beyond default.

questions.title: Application Modernization
questions.scenario: A legacy monolithic application needs modernization. The team wants to incrementally refactor to microservices while maintaining the existing application.
questions.questionText: What pattern enables incremental modernization?

choices.text: Strangler Fig pattern with API gateway routing between legacy and new services
Lift and shift only
Complete rewrite before any deployment
Parallel operation of two completely separate systems

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which modernization pattern lets you peel off monolith features one at a time while the legacy system keeps running?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: The Strangler Fig pattern incrementally replaces monolith components with microservices. An API gateway (Azure API Management) routes requests: new functionality to microservices, remaining to monolith. Over time, the monolith shrinks until fully replaced.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Start with features that are well-defined, high-value, or need scaling.
  • Anti-corruption layer translates between old and new data models.
  • Event-driven integration decouples services during transition.
  • Use feature flags to control traffic routing during migration.

questions.title: Cost Management Architecture
questions.scenario: An organization needs to allocate cloud costs to business units, set budgets with alerts, and identify optimization opportunities across 100 subscriptions.
questions.questionText: What cost management architecture should you implement?

choices.text: Single subscription with manual cost tracking
No tags with estimation-based allocation
Third-party cost tool without Azure integration
Mandatory tags for cost allocation, Cost Management budgets and alerts, and Azure Advisor

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How do you attribute costs to business units, get alerts before budgets are exceeded, and find right-sizing opportunities?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enforce mandatory tags (CostCenter, Department, Project) via Azure Policy. Cost Management groups and filters costs by tags for showback/chargeback. Set budgets at subscription or resource group level with alerts. Azure Advisor identifies right-sizing and reserved instance opportunities.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Cost Management + Billing: analyze spending, create budgets, export data.
  • Budget alerts can trigger Action Groups for automated responses.
  • Reserved Instances and Savings Plans reduce costs for predictable workloads.
  • FinOps practices combine people, process, and technology for cost optimization.

questions.title: IoT Solution Architecture
questions.scenario: A manufacturing company needs to collect telemetry from 100,000 factory devices, process data for anomaly detection, store data for analytics, and send commands back to devices.
questions.questionText: What is the core Azure service for this IoT architecture?

choices.text: Azure IoT Hub with device provisioning, twins, and direct methods
Event Hubs only
Direct HTTP calls to each device
Azure Service Bus for all device communication

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Azure service supports bidirectional communication with 100K devices, including cloud-to-device commands and state management?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure IoT Hub provides device-to-cloud telemetry ingestion, cloud-to-device commands (direct methods), device twins for state management, and Device Provisioning Service for zero-touch enrollment. Route telemetry to Stream Analytics for anomaly detection and storage for analytics.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Device twins: JSON documents representing device state and desired configuration.
  • Direct methods: synchronous request-response calls to devices.
  • IoT Edge runs intelligence at the edge with modules deployed from IoT Hub.
  • Device Provisioning Service enables zero-touch, secure provisioning at scale.

questions.title: Machine Learning Operations
questions.scenario: A data science team needs to train, deploy, and monitor ML models at scale with versioning, reproducibility, and automated retraining.
questions.questionText: Which platform provides end-to-end MLOps capabilities?

choices.text: Custom Python scripts on VMs
Azure Databricks only without model management
Jupyter notebooks without version control
Azure Machine Learning with pipelines, model registry, and managed endpoints

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which platform provides experiment tracking, a model registry, reproducible training pipelines, and managed deployment endpoints?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Machine Learning provides experiment tracking, reproducible pipelines, model versioning in the registry, managed online/batch endpoints for deployment, and monitoring for drift detection. Integrate with Azure DevOps or GitHub for CI/CD of ML workflows.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Pipelines: reusable, schedulable workflows for data prep, training, evaluation.
  • Environments ensure reproducibility with Docker containers.
  • Managed endpoints handle scaling, blue-green deployment, and traffic splitting.
  • Data drift monitoring triggers retraining when model accuracy degrades.

questions.title: Well-Architected Review
questions.scenario: Before going to production, you need to validate that your architecture follows Azure best practices across reliability, security, cost, operations, and performance.
questions.questionText: What framework and tools should guide your review?

choices.text: Azure Well-Architected Framework with Well-Architected Review assessment
Skip review and deploy directly
Only focus on cost optimization
Custom checklist without industry standards

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Microsoft framework organizes best practices into five pillars and offers an assessment tool for actionable recommendations?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: The Azure Well-Architected Framework provides best practices across five pillars: Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, and Performance Efficiency. The Well-Architected Review assessment tool generates recommendations based on your workload's characteristics.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Workload-specific assessments available (AKS, SAP, Azure VMware Solution).
  • Azure Advisor provides automated Well-Architected recommendations.
  • Mission-critical workloads have additional design methodology.
  • Conduct reviews before production and periodically thereafter.

gl-landing-zone.name: Landing Zone
gl-landing-zone.definition: A pre-configured Azure environment with networking, identity, governance, and security foundations for workload deployment.
gl-landing-zone.examNote: Azure Landing Zone accelerators provide reference implementations for enterprise-scale adoption.

gl-hub-spoke.name: Hub-Spoke Topology
gl-hub-spoke.definition: Network architecture with centralized shared services in a hub VNet connected to isolated workload spoke VNets via peering.
gl-hub-spoke.examNote: Use UDRs to force spoke-to-spoke traffic through the hub for inspection.

gl-pim.name: Privileged Identity Management
gl-pim.definition: Azure AD feature providing just-in-time privileged access with approval workflows, time-limited activation, and audit trails.
gl-pim.examNote: Reduces standing access risk; requires Entra ID P2 license.

gl-private-endpoint.name: Private Endpoint
gl-private-endpoint.definition: Network interface with private IP that connects to Azure PaaS services, keeping traffic on the Azure backbone.
gl-private-endpoint.examNote: Requires Private DNS zones for name resolution to private IPs.

gl-cmk.name: Customer-Managed Keys
gl-cmk.definition: Encryption keys stored in customer's Key Vault, providing control over encryption key lifecycle for Azure services.
gl-cmk.examNote: Enables key rotation, revocation, and compliance with key management requirements.

gl-synapse-link.name: Azure Synapse Link
gl-synapse-link.definition: Near-real-time replication from operational databases (Cosmos DB, SQL) to Synapse Analytics for hybrid transactional/analytical processing.
gl-synapse-link.examNote: Eliminates ETL for analytics on operational data; no impact on transactional workload.

gl-strangler-fig.name: Strangler Fig Pattern
gl-strangler-fig.definition: Application modernization pattern that incrementally replaces monolith components with microservices using an API gateway for routing.
gl-strangler-fig.examNote: Enables gradual modernization without big-bang rewrites.

gl-composite-sla.name: Composite SLA
gl-composite-sla.definition: Overall availability calculated by multiplying SLAs of dependent services in series; parallel redundancy improves composite SLA.
gl-composite-sla.examNote: More dependent components = lower composite SLA; design redundancy accordingly.
